models_evaluated: 11 LLMs (names not given in the text)

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic behavior when clinical evidence is released incrementally across turns rather than in a single turn
links.effect: Over 55% of answers were committed within the first two turns. Salient evidence such as lab results triggered premature answering even when models were told to wait. Premature commitment caused accuracy drops of up to 23.3%.
links.quote: We translate these findings into clinically actionable guidance: deferring the diagnostic question to later turns reduces premature answering and improves accuracy at the first point of commitment by up to 62.6%, while reserving salient clinical evidence for later turns prevents a catastrophic accuracy drop of up to 23.3% caused by premature commitment.

unlisted_practices: Deferring the diagnostic question to later turns to reduce premature answering
Reserving salient clinical evidence for later turns in multi-turn diagnostic prompting

screen.practice: deferring diagnostic question and withholding salient evidence to later turns (prompt/interaction design)
screen.reason: The study develops a multi-turn clinical diagnostic benchmark (MINT) and tests prompt/interaction sequencing practices (deferring the diagnostic question and reserving salient evidence to later turns to prevent premature commitment).
